title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: production traces and canary runs showed tail latency regressions under mixed-priority workloads (small low-latency requests being starved by large batching jobs). This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention, and expose conservative timeout knobs. Changes include: 1) strict per-priority queue admission with dynamic credits to prevent long-running sessions from indefinitely consuming the batcher; 2) time-based starvation detection that temporarily boosts scheduling weight for starved queues; 3) bounded wait-time timeouts that eject requests back to the client or to a lower-cost path after configurable thresholds; 4) small kernel scheduling changes to avoid head-of-line blocking when a single large request is waiting for KV cache population; 5) added integration and stress tests, benchmarks and rollout playbook. Performance: canary on prod-dedicated cluster showed 90th percentile token latency improved by ~18% for low-priority small requests under mixed load, and starvation incidents dropped from 22/hour to 0 over a 6-hour stress run. Backwards compatibility: behavior is opt-in via runtime config defaults matching current behavior; the default rollout flips the conservative flags via feature flags. Rollout plan: gradual rollout to dedicated clusters over 48h with canary on 5% of traffic, monitor "continuous_batcher.queue.starvation" and P99 token latency alerts. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] benchmark scripts - [x] docs/console knobs - [x] feature-flag gated rollout - [x] added metrics and tracing spans. Related: builds on prior scheduler tuning work (see PRs: pr-21087, pr-28321).
